questions.question: What is the specific field of study focused on examining extinct animals?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Paleontology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paleontology** is the specific field of study that focuses on the examination of **extinct animals** and other organisms through their fossil remains.
 
• It involves the study of **fossils**, which include preserved remains, impressions, or traces of organisms from the past.
 
• Paleontology bridges the fields of **biology** and **geology** to understand the evolutionary history of life on Earth.
 
• Key tools in paleontology include techniques from **stratigraphy, radiometric dating, and comparative anatomy**.
 
• Paleontologists study extinct species to gain insights into **evolutionary processes, environmental changes, and extinction events.**
 
• It includes specialized subfields such as **vertebrate paleontology** (focused on animals with backbones) and **invertebrate paleontology** (focused on animals without backbones).
 
• Paleontology contributes to understanding phenomena such as the extinction of **dinosaurs** and the emergence of **mammals.**
 
• Famous discoveries in paleontology include fossils of **Tyrannosaurus rex, Archaeopteryx**, and early hominids like **Australopithecus.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gerontology**__

 __
 
• **Gerontology** is the study of aging and older adults, focusing on biological, psychological, and social aspects.
 
• It aims to improve the quality of life and well-being of the elderly through research and practical applications.
 
• Gerontology often overlaps with medical fields such as **geriatrics**, which deals with healthcare for the elderly.
 
 
 
• **Economic Geology**__
 __
 
• **Economic geology** focuses on the study of materials that can be used for economic and industrial purposes, such as **minerals, fossil fuels, and metals.**
 
• It examines the processes of formation, location, extraction, and utilization of **natural resources.**
 
• This field is crucial for understanding and managing **mining operations and energy resources.**
 
 
 
• **Glaciology**__
 
 
• **Glaciology** is the study of glaciers, ice sheets, and other forms of ice in the natural environment.
 
• It focuses on the processes of **ice formation, movement, and melting.**
 
• Glaciology plays a vital role in understanding **climate change** and its impact on sea levels and ecosystems.

questions.question: In which of the following years was India the host of Women's T20 World Cup Cricket?

__

• This tournament marked a significant milestone in **women’s cricket**, as it was held simultaneously with the men’s event, garnering more attention and promoting women’s cricket on a global stage.
 
• The final match of the **2016 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup** was held at the **Eden Gardens in Kolkata**, one of the most iconic cricket stadiums in the world.
 
• **West Indies Women** won the tournament by defeating **Australia Women** in the final, claiming their first-ever ICC Women’s T20 title.
 
• This tournament highlighted the growing interest and investment in **women's sports** and the efforts to bring gender parity in cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **2014**__
 __

• Australia Women clinched the title by defeating **England Women** in the final once again, continuing their dominance in women’s cricket.

questions.question: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded in Lucknow in April _______ with Swami Sahjanand Saraswati as the president.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1936**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All-India Kisan Sabha** (AIKS) was founded in **April 1936** at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The formation of AIKS was driven by the need to address issues concerning **land rights, rural exploitation, and agrarian reforms.**
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**, a prominent leader of farmers and peasants, was elected as the first president of the AIKS.
 
• The Sabha aimed to mobilize farmers, peasants, and agricultural workers for their **socio-economic and political rights**.
 
• It became closely associated with the **Indian National Congress** and played a significant role in the **freedom struggle**.
 
• The organization was instrumental in various **peasant movements**, particularly in regions like Bihar, Bengal, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• One of its key objectives was to abolish the **zamindari system** and secure fair land distribution for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**__

 __
 
• He was a prominent leader of the **peasant movement** in India and is often referred to as the **founder of the Kisan Sabha movement.**
 
• Sahajanand Saraswati authored several books, including **'Mera Jeevan Sangharsh' (My Life Struggle)**, which outlines his experiences and struggles for farmers' rights.
 
• He advocated for the abolition of the **zamindari system** and equal rights for peasants.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**__
 
 
• The **Indian National Congress (INC)** was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• The INC provided a platform for the formation of several organizations, including the **All-India Kisan Sabha**, to address specific societal and economic issues.
 
• Its session in **Lucknow (1936)** was significant as it highlighted the necessity of addressing rural and agrarian problems.

questions.question:
Match the columns:

 
 

 **Plant Group (A)**
 **Example (B)**
 
 

 i. Bryophyta
 a. Rose
 
 

 ii. Pteridophyta
 b. Pine
 
 

 iii. Gymnosperms
 
 
c. Mosses

 
 
 

 iv. Angiosperms
 d. Selaginella
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.__

__
 
• **Bryophyta** are **non-vascular plants** commonly called **mosses.** They do not have true roots, stems, or leaves, and reproduce through spores. These plants typically grow in **moist and shaded **environments.
 
• **Pteridophyta** are **vascular plants **that also reproduce via spores but do not produce seeds. **Selaginella** is a typical example of this group, belonging to **lycophytes.**
 
• **Gymnosperms** are **vascular seed-producing plants** whose seeds are exposed (not enclosed within an ovary).** Pine** is a classic gymnosperm characterized by needle-like leaves and cone-based reproduction.
 
• **Angiosperms** are** flowering plants** that produce seeds enclosed within fruits. Roses are typical angiosperms, distinguished by their flowers, broad leaves, and fruit formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophyta **(mosses) are among the oldest land plants, having appeared around 450 million years ago. They lack specialized vascular tissues like xylem and phloem, relying on diffusion to move water and nutrients. Ecologically, they play a vital role in preventing soil erosion and retaining moisture.
 
• **Pteridophyta **(including Selaginella) possess vascular tissues, allowing them to grow taller than bryophytes. They reproduce through spores produced in sporangia. Other examples include ferns, horsetails, and club mosses.
 
• **Gymnosperms **(such as pine) are mostly evergreen trees and shrubs with needle-like leaves. Their seeds develop on the surface of scales or leaves that are often modified into cones. They include economically important species like pine, fir, spruce, and cedar, which are valued for timber and resin.
 
• **Angiosperms **(like rose) represent the largest and most diverse group of plants. They have flowers as their reproductive organs and produce fruits that enclose seeds. Angiosperms are further divided into monocots and dicots based on leaf venation, seed structure, and flower parts.

questions.question: As per the Periodic Labour Force data 2023, which of the following states recorded the highest unemployment rate in urban areas for the age group 15 years and above?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023**, **Himachal Pradesh** recorded the **highest unemployment rate** in urban areas for individuals aged **15 years and above**.
 
• The PLFS is conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India.
 
• Himachal Pradesh, despite being a state with a strong tourism sector and agricultural base, has faced challenges in generating sufficient employment opportunities in **urban regions**.
 
• Urban areas in Himachal Pradesh have experienced a rise in unemployment due to limited industrial development and dependency on seasonal industries such as tourism.
 
• **Unemployment rate** refers to the percentage of persons in the labour force who are unemployed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chhattisgarh**__

 __
 
• Chhattisgarh has a predominantly **rural economy**, and unemployment rates in urban areas are generally lower compared to other states.
 
• It is known for its **mining and mineral resources** and has contributed significantly to the industrial sector.
 
• Employment opportunities in Chhattisgarh are largely driven by its **agriculture and forestry-based industries.**
 
 
 
• **Rajasthan**__
 __
 
• Rajasthan has a significant portion of its economy dependent on **tourism, handicrafts, and agriculture.**
 
• Urban unemployment in Rajasthan is generally moderate, but challenges arise due to the state's **arid climate and limited industrial base.**
 
• Rajasthan has also focused on promoting **start-ups and entrepreneurship** to address unemployment issues.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**__
 
 
• Kerala has a high literacy rate and a significant diaspora population, which has contributed to its **economic growth.**
 
• Urban unemployment in Kerala is influenced by the state's dependence on **remittances and service-based industries.**
 
• Despite the challenges, Kerala has made strides in sectors like **information technology and health care.**

questions.question: The Sun Temple at Konark, the Khajuraho Temple in Madhya Pradesh and the recently constructed Ram Temple in Ayodhya are examples of temples designed in which style of temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Nagara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nagara style** is one of the three major styles of temple architecture in India, the other two being the **Dravida** and **Vesara**.
 
• This style originated and flourished in **North India**, particularly in regions such as **Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Gujarat**.
 
• The **Sun Temple at Konark** in Odisha, the **Khajuraho Temples** in Madhya Pradesh, and the recently constructed **Ram Temple** in Ayodhya are prime examples of this architectural style.
 
• The Nagara style is characterized by its **curvilinear shikhara (spire)** that rises vertically above the sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• Temples in this style are constructed on a **raised platform** or base, called the **jagati**.
 
• It features intricate carvings and sculptures depicting scenes from **Hindu mythology**, gods, goddesses, and celestial beings.
 
• Unlike the Dravida style, the Nagara temples do not have an elaborate boundary wall or gateway (gopuram) and are often open to the surroundings.
 
• The Nagara style temples are further classified into various sub-styles based on regional differences, such as the **Kalinga style** in Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vesara**__

 __
 
• The **Vesara style** is a fusion of the **Nagara** and **Dravida** architectural styles.
 
• This style is prominent in regions such as **Karnataka** and areas governed by the **Chalukyas**.
 
• Examples of Vesara style temples include the **Badami Cave Temples** and the **Pattadakal Temples**.
 
 
 
• **Hoysala**__
 __
 
• The **Hoysala style** evolved during the reign of the **Hoysala dynasty** in Karnataka (12th–13th century).
 
• It is known for its **star-shaped platforms**, intricate carvings, and **soapstone material**.
 
• Prominent examples include the **Chennakeshava Temple at Belur** and the **Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu**.
 
 
 
• **Dravida**__
 
 
• The **Dravida style** is associated with **South India**, particularly Tamil Nadu.
 
• It features **pyramidal gopurams (gateway towers)**, large temple complexes, and water tanks.
 
• Examples include the **Brihadeeswara Temple** in Thanjavur and the **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai.

questions.question: Which of the following leaders died after being hit by sticks while protesting against the Simon Commission?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent Indian freedom fighter, known as the "**Punjab Kesari**" or "**The Lion of Punjab**."
 
• He played a key role in the **Indian Independence Movement** and was a leader of the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio** (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal).
 
• He protested against the **Simon Commission** in 1928, which was boycotted by Indians because it did not include any Indian representatives.
 
• During a protest in **Lahore**, he suffered severe injuries due to a brutal lathi charge by the police led by **James A. Scott**.
 
• He succumbed to his injuries on **November 17, 1928**, and his death became a rallying cry for Indian freedom fighters.
 
• His sacrifice inspired other revolutionaries like **Bhagat Singh** to take up the cause for India's independence.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was also an author and social reformer, contributing significantly to the upliftment of Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandra Shekhar Azad**__

 __
 
• **Chandra Shekhar Azad** was an iconic revolutionary who played a critical role in the **Indian independence movement**.
 
• He was associated with the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** and worked alongside **Bhagat Singh** and other revolutionaries.
 
• Azad vowed never to be captured alive by the British and died in a shootout at **Alfred Park** in Allahabad in **1931**.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__
 __
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was a prominent leader in the **Indian National Movement** and a member of the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio**.
 
• He is known for his slogan "**Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it**."
 
• Tilak contributed significantly to the revival of Indian culture and promoted festivals like **Ganesh Chaturthi** and **Shivaji Jayanti** to unite Indians.
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh**__
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a revolutionary freedom fighter who advocated for **armed resistance** against British rule.
 
• He was deeply inspired by the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai** and participated in the assassination of **John Saunders**, believing him to be responsible for Rai's death.
 
• Bhagat Singh was executed in **1931** for his revolutionary activities and remains a symbol of courage and sacrifice.

questions.question: NISHTHA stands for ____________

options.text: National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Assessment
National Inauguration for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement
National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement
National Inauguration for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Assessment

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NISHTHA** stands for **National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement**.
 
• It is a flagship program of the **Ministry of Education, Government of India**.
 
• The initiative aims to build the **capacities of teachers and school heads** at the elementary level across the country.
 
• NISHTHA focuses on improving the **quality of school education** through integrated teacher training.
 
• The program emphasizes **training on various aspects of education**, such as **competency-based learning, inclusive education, health and well-being, and environmental conservation.**
 
• NISHTHA leverages **technology and digital resources** to make training accessible and effective.
 
• It plays a critical role in the implementation of the **New Education Policy (NEP) 2020**.
 
• The initiative is an effort to foster **holistic development** among students by empowering educators with modern teaching techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• National Education Policy (NEP) 2019:

 
 
• The NEP 2019 is a comprehensive framework to guide the development of education in the country. It covers elementary to higher education in both rural and urban India.
 
• The policy emphasizes the importance of early childhood care and education (ECCE), foundational literacy and numeracy, and the overall development of students.
 
• It proposes a new curricular structure, which includes a 5+3+3+4 design, corresponding to the ages 3-8 years (Foundational Stage), 8-11 (Preparatory Stage), 11-14 (Middle Stage), and 14-18 (Secondary Stage).
 
• The policy also focuses on teacher education and training, setting up a National Higher Education Regulatory Authority (NHERA), and promoting the use of technology in education.

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles is Right to Equality mentioned?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Articles 14-18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Equality** is enshrined under **Articles 14 to 18** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is one of the fundamental rights guaranteed to all citizens of India, ensuring **equality before the law** and equal protection under the law.
 
• **Article 14** establishes the principle of equality before the law and prohibits discrimination by the State.
 
• **Article 15** prohibits discrimination on grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth**.
 
• **Article 16** guarantees equality of opportunity in matters related to public employment.
 
• **Article 17** abolishes **untouchability** and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18** prohibits the State from conferring any **titles**, except for military or academic distinctions.
 
• These provisions collectively ensure that every individual is treated equally in all aspects of governance and society, fostering a sense of fairness and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles 1-4**__

 __
 
• These articles deal with the **Union and its territory**.
 
• **Article 1** defines India as a Union of States.
 
• **Article 2** empowers Parliament to admit new states into the Union or establish new states.
 
• **Article 3** provides for the formation of new states and alteration of existing states’ boundaries with Parliamentary approval.
 
• **Article 4** specifies that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 will not be considered amendments to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Articles 10-12**__
 __
 
• These articles fall under Part II of the Constitution, which deals with **Citizenship**.
 
• **Article 10** ensures that every individual continues to enjoy citizenship as per constitutional provisions.
 
• **Article 11** empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship through legislation.
 
• **Article 12** defines the term **State**, which includes the Government and Parliament of India, State Legislatures, and local authorities.
 
 
 
• **Articles 19-22**__
 
 
• These articles are part of the **Right to Freedom**, guaranteed under the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 19** provides for six fundamental freedoms, including freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• **Article 20** protects individuals in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• **Article 21** guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• **Article 22** provides protections related to detention and arrest.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints the Acting Chief Justice in the absence of the Chief Justice of India?

options.text: Senior most Judge of the Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India** appoints an **Acting Chief Justice** in the absence of the **Chief Justice of India (CJI).**
 
• This provision is made under **Article 126** of the **Indian Constitution**, which deals with the designation of an Acting Chief Justice.
 
• The **Acting Chief Justice** is usually the **senior-most judge** of the **Supreme Court**, ensuring continuity in the judiciary's functioning.
 
• The appointment is essential to ensure that the **Supreme Court** functions smoothly even in the absence of the **CJI**.
 
• The **President** acts on the recommendation of the **Union Government** while making such appointments.
 
• This mechanism ensures that the **judiciary** remains independent and operational at all times, maintaining the balance of power within the government framework.
 
• The role of the Acting Chief Justice is temporary and ceases once the **CJI** resumes office or a new **CJI** is appointed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Role of Chief Justice of India

 
 
• The Chief Justice is responsible for the allocation of work to other judges.
 
• The Chief Justice administers the oath of office to the President In the absence of the President and the Vice-President, the Chief Justice sits as the Acting President of India
 
• The Chief Justice is the ex-officio Chancellor of most autonomous law schools in India.
 
 
 
• Eligibility
 
 
• The individual must be a citizen of India.
 
• The person must not exceed 65 years of age.
 
• In order to be eligible to be Chief Justice of India, the person must serve as a judge at High Court for at least five years or the person should be an advocate in the High court or the Supreme court for at least 10 years or a distinguished jurist.

questions.question: The condition when the amount of dissolved oxygen in a water body is alarmingly decreased is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypoxia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypoxia** refers to the condition where the amount of **dissolved oxygen** in a water body is alarmingly low, making it difficult for aquatic life to survive.
 
• This typically occurs in areas where there is an excess of **organic pollutants or nutrient enrichment**, leading to phenomena like **eutrophication**.
 
• The lack of oxygen is harmful to aquatic organisms such as **fish, invertebrates, and plants**, which depend on oxygen for survival.
 
• Hypoxia is commonly observed in areas termed as **"dead zones,”** such as the Gulf of Mexico, where oxygen levels are insufficient for sustaining marine life.
 
• The primary causes include **agricultural runoff** (rich in fertilizers), **industrial discharge**, and **sewage effluents**.
 
• It is a critical environmental issue as it disrupts the **aquatic ecosystem**, affects biodiversity, and has economic implications for fisheries.
 
• Prevention and mitigation strategies include reducing nutrient pollution, improving wastewater treatment, and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypothermia**__

 __
 
• **Hypothermia** is a medical condition where the body loses heat faster than it can produce, leading to an abnormally low **body temperature.**
 
• It is caused by prolonged exposure to **cold temperatures** and can result in fatigue, confusion, and in severe cases, organ failure or death.
 
 
 
• **Anoxia**__
 __
 
• **Anoxia** is the complete absence of **oxygen** in a given environment, often leading to the death of organisms.
 
• It is more severe than hypoxia and can occur in both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Acidification**__
 
 
• **Acidification** refers to the process where water bodies become more acidic due to the absorption of **carbon dioxide (CO2)** or other pollutants.
 
• This phenomenon, commonly termed **ocean acidification**, has detrimental effects on marine life, particularly on organisms with calcium carbonate shells or skeletons.

questions.question: In Union Budget 2023-24, an aspirational Blocks Programme covering how many blocks has been launched?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**500 Blocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aspirational Blocks Programme** is a newly launched initiative under the **Union Budget 2023-24**.
 
• This program aims to cover **500 blocks** across the country.
 
• The focus is on enhancing the **developmental outcomes** in these blocks through targeted interventions.
 
• It is designed to address **critical developmental gaps** and improve the quality of life for citizens residing in these blocks.
 
• The program builds upon the success of the earlier **Aspirational Districts Programme**, which aimed to transform **underdeveloped districts**.

• This program is in line with India’s commitment to achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** by 2030.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the chemical formula for sulphur hexafluoride?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**SF6.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6)** is an inorganic, colorless, odorless, non-flammable, and non-toxic gas.
 
• The chemical formula **SF6** represents a molecule consisting of one **sulfur (S)** atom and six **fluorine (F)** atoms.
 
• It belongs to the class of compounds known as **hexafluorides**, where six fluorine atoms are bonded to a central atom.
 
• **Sulphur hexafluoride** is widely used as an insulating gas in high-voltage electrical equipment such as **circuit breakers, switchgear, and transformers**.
 
• Its exceptional dielectric properties make it highly effective in preventing electrical discharges.
 
• It is also utilized in the production of **semiconductors** and in various **scientific applications** such as tracer gas studies.
 
• SF6 is considered a **greenhouse gas** with a high global warming potential, and its use is regulated to minimize environmental impact.
 
• The structure of SF6 is **octahedral**, meaning the six fluorine atoms are symmetrically arranged around the central sulfur atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **S2F6**__

 __
 
• **S2F6** is not the correct formula for sulphur hexafluoride. It represents a different chemical compound, **disulfur hexafluoride**, where two sulfur atoms are bonded together with six fluorine atoms.
 
• **Disulfur hexafluoride** is much less common than SF6 and has different chemical and physical properties.
 
 
 
• **SF2**__
 __
 
• **SF** represents sulphur difluoride, which consists of one sulfur atom bonded to two fluorine atoms. It is different from sulphur hexafluoride.
 
• SF____2 __is not widely used as an insulating gas and does not exhibit the same dielectric properties as SF6.
 
 
 
• __**S6F**__
 
 
• **S6F** is not a valid chemical formula. It does not correspond to any known stable compound and is likely an incorrect representation.

• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **Vaishnavite traditions** and is influenced by the **spiritual themes of Lord Krishna and Radha.**
 
• Compositions in **Meitei language**, the primary language spoken in Manipur, are an integral part of Manipuri dance performances.
 
• It is characterized by its **graceful movements**, **soft hand gestures**, and the use of unique costumes like the traditional **Kumil** (long skirts).
 
• Manipuri dance involves themes from the **Raas Leela**, representing the divine love between Radha and Krishna, and other mythological stories.
 
• The dance form is known for its **delicate and lyrical expression**, making it distinct from other Indian classical dances.
 
• It is performed during important festivals like **Janmashtami** and **Rath Yatra** in Manipur.
 
• Manipuri dance emphasizes a strong connection between **spirituality** and **artistic expression**.

• Bharatanatyam is renowned for its intricate **footwork**, **expressive gestures**, and **spiritual themes**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Iron Age?

1. The establishment of large cities took place on the basis of sizeable surplus.

2. The ceramic associated with this age was Painted Grey Ware.

3. The Indus Valley Civilization flourished during the Iron Age
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iron Age** was marked by the widespread use of iron for tools and weapons, leading to advancements in agriculture, warfare, and urbanization.
 
• The **establishment of large cities** during this age was driven by the production of a **sizeable surplus** of agricultural products, which supported large populations and urban settlements.
 
• The **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)** ceramic is a significant archaeological marker of the Iron Age in the Indian subcontinent. This type of pottery is associated with the later Vedic period and reflects the cultural and economic activities of the time.
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization**, however, predates the Iron Age. It flourished during the Chalcolithic (Copper Age) and Bronze Age, making the third statement in the question incorrect.
 
• The Iron Age in the Indian subcontinent is characterized by the **emergence of early kingdoms**, the development of metallurgy, and the increasing complexity of societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)**__

 __
 
• **PGW pottery** is associated with the later Vedic period and was found in archaeological sites across North India, including regions of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Rajasthan.
 
• This type of pottery is generally wheel-made, with a grey surface and black or red painted designs.
 
• It reflects the development of a settled agricultural society and the use of iron tools during the Iron Age.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**__
 __
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** existed during the Chalcolithic and Bronze Age, from approximately 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
 
• It was known for its advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and architecture.
 
• This civilization predates the Iron Age, which began around 1200 BCE in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age Characteristics**__
 
 
• The Iron Age is marked by the introduction and use of **iron tools** and weapons, which were stronger and more durable than their bronze counterparts.
 
• It led to significant advancements in **agriculture, warfare, and societal organization**.
 
• It saw the rise of early states and kingdoms, as well as the development of **trade networks**.
